strings.name: Novak Djokovic
strings.role: Tennis player · Grand Slam and Olympic champion
strings.summary: Djokovic became a leading figure in men’s tennis through versatility across surfaces and sustained performance. He won 24 Grand Slam singles titles and completed a career Golden Slam with Olympic gold in Paris. His 428 weeks at world No. 1 demonstrate his longevity. He continued competing on tour in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected events extend through October 2026. Records concern completed competition. A career Golden Slam does not mean winning every title in the same year.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: 24 Grand Slam titles
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: His 2023 US Open victory brought his Grand Slam singles total to 24.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Career Golden Slam
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Olympic singles gold in 2024 completed his career collection of all four majors and the Olympic title.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: World No. 1 records
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: Spent 428 weeks atop the ATP rankings and finished eight seasons as year-end No. 1.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: 102nd tour title
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Won the China Open in Beijing after finalist Alex de Minaur retired with an injury.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Reaches 100 titles
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Defeated Hubert Hurkacz in the Geneva final to win his 100th tour-level singles title.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Olympic singles gold
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Beat Carlos Alcaraz in the Paris final to complete a career Golden Slam.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: 24th Grand Slam title
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Defeated Daniil Medvedev in the US Open final.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Completes career Grand Slam
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Won Roland-Garros for the first time, holding all four major singles titles simultaneously.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: First reaches No. 1
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Rose to the top of the ATP singles rankings after winning his first Wimbledon title.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: First Grand Slam title
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Defeated Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in the Australian Open final.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Turns professional
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Entered professional tennis, progressing from junior competition to the tour.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Belgrade
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in what was then Yugoslavia; later represented Serbia.
